title: Galaxy rotation curve recompute from pinned public tables (NGC 3198)

amendments.text:
## AMENDMENTS

(none at freeze)

- 2026-10-04T03:1xZ, parser only, no claim or threshold changed. Table1 (`SPARC_Lelli2016c.mrt`)
  declares a 113-byte fixed-width layout with Vflat at bytes 87-91, but all 175 data rows are
  131 bytes and the fields sit at other offsets. A byte-offset read failed on NGC 3198
  (`ValueError: could not convert string to float: '5  13.'`). Every row splits into exactly
  19 whitespace fields in the declared label order, so Table1 is parsed by whitespace. The
  frozen-at-writing sha256 of this file (before this amendment) was
  47209b9d0a446201ca8564d4487287578bcc52022eb925ecc8f1cdd551ce722d.

run.id: SCI-R0 recompute (one galaxy, one telescope file)

rerun.detail: The script that computed the result is not in this tree. Its inputs are public SPARC files from astroweb.case.edu, named by sha256 in results/scratch/recompute-result.json and not redistributed here.

rows.claim: C1: the observed curve is flat within 10 km/s beyond 10 kpc

bar.text: C1: PASS if max over rows beyond R of |V_obs - median| <= 10 km/s; INSUFFICIENT if fewer than 5 rows

rows.note: a demonstration, not a blind test: the thresholds were set by someone expecting a PASS

rows.claim: C2: the observed velocity exceeds the baryonic prediction by at least 30 km/s at every row beyond 10 kpc

bar.text: C2: PASS if min over rows beyond R of (V_obs - V_bar) >= 30 km/s

rows.claim: C3: the published V_flat replays from the rows within 1 km/s
telescope file header checks passing (FITS and pipeline conventions)
rows.note: descriptive: no preregistered bar; checks and tolerances written before running, outside the prereg; differs from the report (22 of 24)

misses.description: the published SPARC Table1 does not match its own byte layout: the header declares 113-byte rows with Vflat at bytes 87-91, every data row is 131 bytes, and standard readers fail; read by whitespace as a stated parser-only amendment

two header keywords state the same pixel area to different precision (relative difference 1.1e-4 against a tolerance of 1e-5 set before running); finding or tolerance choice is a ruleset-design question
no CHECKSUM or DATASUM on any header unit of the telescope file (an optional convention); integrity rests on the archive's md5, which matches
the pipeline documentation says ERR combines two variance terms; in the file ERR squared equals the sum of three (VAR_FLAT included) to 2.9e-7, and the two-term form misses by up to 3.9%

label: demo
findings: "telescope file header checks passing (FITS and pipeline conventions)": computed 23 of 25 from the results; the run's report states 22 of 24
